Section 7—Regulation FD 

Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure 

On October 28, 2026, in connection with its 2026 Investor Day, Oracle Corporation (“Oracle”) issued a press release regarding its strategy and financial guidance, as well as certain other matters. A copy of the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 
8-K
 and is incorporated herein by reference. The information set forth in this Item 7.01 and in the attached Exhibit 99.1 shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or the Exchange Act, except as shall be expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing.

Oracle Investor Day 2026: Accelerating Value Creation 

•

Set long-term outlook for FY30 
of

$225 billion+ in total revenue, representing more than 35% CAGR from
FY26, 
non-GAAP
 operating margin of 40%+ and 
non-GAAP
 EPS $21+. 

•

Defined timeline to positive free cash flow 
during the second half of FY28 and set free cash flow target of $30
billion+ for FY29. 

•

Committed to limiting additional capital raises through FY30
 to $20 billion, excluding refinancing of
existing debt, split between $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt. 

•

Confirmed that growth will be self-funded beginning in FY29 
and net debt to adjusted EBITDA will be below 3.5
times in FY29.¹

AUSTIN, Texas, October
 28, 2026 — 
Oracle Corporation (NYSE: ORCL) today hosted an
Investor Day in Las Vegas, NV. At the event 
co-CEO
 Clay Magouryk, 
co-CEO
 Mike Sicilia and CFO Hilary Maxson presented and responded to questions about the
company’s strategy and updated medium-term financial guidance. 

At its Investor Day, Oracle described how its unique portfolio positioning across cloud infrastructure, database and
applications is expected to drive total revenue growth of more than 35% CAGR from FY26 through FY30, reaching total revenue of $225 billion or more in FY30. It also outlined its expectations for strong profitability and free cash flow
generation from each of its three business models. Following a period of peak capex in FY27-FY28, capital expenditures are expected to step-down in FY29, supporting positive free cash flow of at least $30 billion in FY29. 

Oracle committed to limiting additional funding to be raised in the capital markets for its FY27-FY30 investment cycle to $20 billion, currently expected to be
$10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt. This incremental funding requirement excludes refinancing of existing debt. This is in addition to the $20 billion

at-the-market
 equity raise completed in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce
upfront cash requirements through the transition to positive free cash flow. 

Oracle reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 outlook for total revenue of at least
$90 billion and 
non-GAAP
 earnings per share of $8.10. The company’s capital allocation priorities remain maintaining investment-grade credit ratings, paying a dividend and funding growth
opportunities. 

The Investor Day presentations and webcast replay will be available on the 
Oracle Investor Day website
. 

1. Net debt includes borrowings, vendor financing, and operating and finance lease liabilities, less cash and marketable securities. Adjusted EBITDA is based on
Oracle’s reported 
non-GAAP
 results, with depreciation and operating lease expense added back. 

About Oracle

Oracle provides cloud applications and infrastructure for enterprises worldwide. For more information about Oracle (NYSE: ORCL), visit www.oracle.com.

Non GAAP Financial Measures 

To supplement our financial results presented on a GAAP basis, we use 
non-GAAP
 measures, which exclude certain significant
expenses including stock-based compensation, expenses related to acquisitions, restructuring and certain other operating expenses, that we believe are helpful in understanding our past financial performance and our future results. Our 
non-GAAP
 financial measures are not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for comparable GAAP measures and should be read only in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in
accordance with GAAP. 

Safe Harbor Statement

revenues and revenue growth, 
non-GAAP
 operating margin and earnings per share; the timing and amount of positive free cash flow; expected capital expenditures; future funding needs and financing strategy,
including Oracle’s commitment to limit additional capital raises; the expected effects of vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments on upfront cash requirements; the timing of self-funded growth; future net debt to
adjusted EBITDA; and capital allocation priorities, including maintaining investment-grade credit ratings, paying dividends and funding growth opportunities, are “forward-looking statements” and are subject to material risks and
uncertainties. Forward-looking statements may be identified by words such as “expect,” “anticipate,” “plan,” “believe,” “intend,” “target,” “will,” and
“committed,” and similar expressions, although not all forward-looking statements contain these words. Risks and uncertainties that could affect our current expectations and our actual results, include, among others: our ability to
develop new products and services, integrate acquired products and services and enhance our existing products and services, including our AI products; our AI products not operating as anticipated; our ability to successfully execute our Oracle Cloud
strategy; our ability to anticipate, plan for, secure and manage datacenter capacity; our management of complex cloud and hardware offerings, including the sourcing of technologies and technology components such as graphic processing units;
significant coding, manufacturing or configuration errors in our offerings; risks associated with acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic alliances; business volatility and risks associated with government contracting; economic, political and
market conditions, including tariffs and trade wars; information technology system failures, privacy and data security concerns; cybersecurity breaches; disruptions from our period workforce restructurings; unfavorable legal proceedings, government
investigations, and complex and changing laws and regulations, including healthcare regulations. A detailed discussion of these factors and other risks that affect our business is contained in our SEC filings, including our most recent reports on
